=================
THE CONTROL PANEL
=================

  Once OrbixERP is on a server, the same window you installed it with becomes
  its control panel. Double-click Remote-Setup.cmd, enter the server details,
  and the wizard notices it is already installed and offers Open control
  panel.

  Everything here happens on the server. You never type a command on it, and
  nothing is installed on your PC.

  To install on a server for the first time, see REMOTE-INSTALL.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

What each button does
=====================

  Button: Is it running?
  What happens on the server: Reports whether each part is up, healthy, and on
      which address
  Safe while people are working?: Yes - reads only

  Button: Recent activity
  What happens on the server: The last 200 lines of the application log
  Safe while people are working?: Yes - reads only

  Button: Back up now
  What happens on the server: Writes a database backup into backups/ on the
      server
  Safe while people are working?: Yes - runs against the live database

  Button: Restart
  What happens on the server: Stops and starts again
  Safe while people are working?: No - a short outage, seconds

  Button: Start the system
  What happens on the server: Starts it and waits until it genuinely answers
  Safe while people are working?: Yes

  Button: Stop the system
  What happens on the server: Shuts down cleanly. Your data is kept.
  Safe while people are working?: No - nobody can use it until started again

  Button: Settings (.env)
  What happens on the server: Opens the server's settings file to read or
      change
  Safe while people are working?: Reading yes; saving needs a restart

  Button: Update to this bundle
  What happens on the server: Upgrades the server to the version in this
      folder
  Safe while people are working?: No - takes a backup first, then a short
      outage

  Button: Open in browser
  What happens on the server: Opens the ERP address on this PC
  Safe while people are working?: Yes

  Each button runs the matching command in the installation folder -
  ./orbixerp.sh status, logs, backup, restart, start, stop, update. Nothing is
  done by a separate mechanism, so a person at the server's own terminal sees
  exactly the same behaviour.

  While a job is running every button is disabled, and the heading shows a
  clock so you can tell the difference between slow and stuck. A database
  backup on a real system is not quick.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Settings (.env)
===============

  Opens the server's .env - the file holding every setting, including its
  passwords. It is read and written straight down the encrypted connection; no
  copy is left on your PC.

  Changes take effect only after a restart. The panel offers one as soon as
  you save.

  Before writing, the previous file is kept on the server as
  .env.bak-<date>-<time>, so a mistyped line can always be put back.

Four lines cannot be changed here
---------------------------------

  ERP_DB_PASSWORD, ERP_DB_MODE, ERP_DB_NAME and ERP_DB_USER are shown but
  refused if edited.

  This is not caution for its own sake. Changing the database password here
  does not change the password on the database - the database already exists
  and keeps the password it was created with. All you would achieve is
  stopping OrbixERP being able to open its own data, and the way back is not
  obvious to somebody who has just locked themselves out. The same is true of
  the database name, its user, and whether it runs in a container or on the
  host.

  If one of those genuinely has to change, it is a job to do deliberately,
  with a backup in hand and the database changed to match. Ask us.

What is worth changing
----------------------

  Setting: ERP_PUBLIC_HOST
  Why you might: The address people use has changed
  Watch out for: With a certificate, it must match the real name or the
      certificate stops matching

  Setting: ERP_HTTP_PORT
  Why you might: Something else already uses that port
  Watch out for: Anyone using the old port has to be told

  Setting: ERP_BIND_ADDR
  Why you might: Restrict which network can reach it
  Watch out for: Bind too narrowly and nobody reaches it at all

  Setting: ERP_TLS_ENABLED
  Why you might: Turn a proper certificate on or off
  Watch out for: Needs a real domain name pointed at the server

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Backups
=======

  Back up now writes into backups/ in the installation folder on the server.
  It runs against the live database, so it is safe during the working day.

  A backup that only exists on the same server is not really a backup. Copy it
  somewhere else - another machine, or storage that is not that server. If the
  server is lost, anything on it is lost with it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Updating
========

  Update to this bundle upgrades the server to the version in the folder you
  launched from. So to update, get a newer bundle from us, unpack it, and run
  its Remote-Setup.cmd.

  The update takes a database backup first and stops if that backup fails.
  Your data, settings and security keys are kept.

  If the server is already on that version, the panel says so and does
  nothing.

  > Database changes only run forwards. Restoring the backup the update names
    is the only way back to the previous version, which is why the update
    refuses to proceed without one.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Restoring a backup is not here
==============================

  Restoring replaces the database: everything recorded since that backup was
  taken is lost. That is not a button anybody should be able to press by
  accident, so it is deliberately left out.

  To restore, someone signs in to the server and runs it by hand - the command
  is in OPERATIONS, and it asks for confirmation before doing anything.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

When something goes wrong
=========================

  What you see: That did not work with messages above
  What it means: The command failed on the server
  What to do: Read the messages; TROUBLESHOOTING covers the usual causes

  What you see: The clock keeps counting on a backup
  What it means: Normal on a large database
  What to do: Leave it; backups take as long as they take

  What you see: Is it running? says unhealthy
  What it means: Started but not answering yet, or failing to start
  What to do: Wait a minute and check again, then Recent activity

  What you see: Nothing responds after a settings change
  What it means: A setting is wrong
  What to do: Re-open Settings, compare with .env.bak-..., put the line back,
      restart

  What you see: The server's identity has changed
  What it means: The server's fingerprint no longer matches
  What to do: Stop. Find out whether it was rebuilt before continuing

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

What this panel will not do
===========================

  It will not delete anything, drop a database, or remove the installation.
  There is no button for any of that, on purpose. Anything genuinely
  destructive is left to a person at a terminal who has had to think about it
  first.
